Graduate Admission
Admission Requirements
The minimum academic requirement for admission to the M.Sc. and Ph.D. programs in Chemistry is normally a high second-class standing (cGPA above 3.00).
Applicants applying directly from a B.Sc. to a Ph.D. without completing an M.Sc. must have a minimum cGPA of 3.7.
Applicants from other institutions must have an academic background equivalent to that of a McGill graduate with an Honours or Major degree in Chemistry or a related field, such as Physics or Biochemistry.
Admission is competitive. The Department receives many applications and can accept only a limited number of students.
Applicants who obtained their degree outside North America should contact the graduate.chemistry [at] mcgill.ca (Graduate Program Administrator) to confirm that they meet the admission requirements.
English Language Proficiency
Applicants must meet McGill's English proficiency requirements.
After your test scores have been sent by the testing centre, please allow 15 business days for the results to be matched to your application.
Required Application Documents
After submitting your initial application and paying the application fee, you will be asked to provide the following documents through the application portal.
Academic Transcripts
Transcripts from every university-level institution you have attended, including institutions from which you received transfer credits.
Transcripts issued in a language other than English or French must include a translation into English or French, prepared by the issuing institution or a certified translator.
The original-language transcript must also be submitted. Translations alone are not sufficient.
Two Letters of Reference
You must provide the names and institutional or organizational email addresses of two referees who are familiar with your academic or professional work and are willing to recommend you.
The reference process works as follows:
Each referee will receive an automated email from McGill's application portal with instructions for submitting a reference.
Referees will log in to a secure McGill website to upload their letters and, where applicable, complete standardized questions.
If a referee declines the request, you will be notified by email and asked to provide an alternate.
You may update referee email addresses, replace referees, or add a new referee through the application portal.
You will receive an automated confirmation when a reference is submitted, and your application checklist will be updated.
Applicants are responsible for ensuring that both references are submitted by the deadline. You may use the portal's “Send a Reminder” feature or contact your referees directly with a polite reminder.
Each letter of reference must meet the following requirements:
Clearly identify the program to which you have applied and provide information to help the Admissions Committee assess your application.
Be dated within the past 12 months.
Include the referee's position or title and full institutional or organizational contact information.
Curriculum Vitae (CV)
Submit an up-to-date CV outlining your academic background, relevant experience, research experience, publications, awards, and other relevant achievements.
Statement of Purpose / Personal Statement
Submit a statement of 1–2 pages describing your experience, motivation for graduate studies, research interests, and career aspirations.
For complete application instructions, visit McGill's Graduate Admissions website.
Application Deadlines
The Department of Chemistry follows a rolling admissions process. Applications are reviewed by an Admissions Committee that meets regularly.
Applicants are encouraged to graduate.chemistry [at] mcgill.ca (contact the Department) for a pre-evaluation before submitting an application.

Choosing a Supervisor and Research Lab
Incoming students are not committed to a supervisor before arriving at the Department of Chemistry.
Students are encouraged to meet with all professors whose research interests them, as well as any professors who request a meeting, before deciding on a supervisor.
In early August, incoming students will receive a list of professors and will be responsible for arranging meetings with them.
These meetings provide an opportunity to:
Explore the breadth of research conducted within the Department.
Learn about available research projects and training opportunities.
Discuss potential co-supervision arrangements.
Meet current graduate students and learn about their experiences.
Students should use this process to explore their options and make an informed decision about their research group and supervisor.
